paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of the number of conversations across different categories regarding the perception of being deceived. The horizontal axis represents the number of conversations, labeled as "Number of Conversations", with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60, marked at intervals of 10. The vertical axis categorizes the data into four labels: "Academic Collaboration", "Recruitment", "Academic Funding", and "Journalism". Each category consists of stacked bars representing the levels of deception: "Yes" (red), "Partially" (yellow), and "No" (green). For "Academic Funding", the "Yes" portion of the bar is the longest, extending close to 70. For "Journalism", the "Partially" segment is prominent, reaching approximately 50. Meanwhile, for "Recruitment" and "Academic Collaboration" the "Yes" section stands out, with "Recruitment" reaching just under 40, and "Academic Collaboration" slightly above 35. The bars are not sorted by value but are visually organized per category, with no additional visual emphasis or annotations observed. A legend is given top left describing the bar and color.
